sites.why: Keyword-count heuristic standing in for a semantic classification into a closed set with a fallback label.

implement.brief: Replace the keyword heuristic in categorize() so the ticket is assigned one of billing, account_access, bug, feature_request, or general.
implement.input_shape: the InboundTicket object passed to categorize()

samples.subject: Charged twice this month
samples.body: My card shows two charges of $49 on the 3rd. I only have one workspace. Can you look into it?

samples.subject: Feedback
samples.body: Loving the product so far, just wanted to say thanks to the team.

rubric.text: Uses one choice question over the five categories (or the four specific ones plus a general/none option) rather than one noul per category recombined in code.
general (or an equivalent no-match option) is available as an answer so tickets that fit nothing are not forced into a specific category.
customerPlan is not sent to the model, since no category depends on it.

sites.why: Prompt-and-parse chat completion whose free-text reply is regex-parsed into a 1 to 5 level, with a silent default on parse failure.

implement.brief: Replace the chat-completion call and regex parsing in rateUrgency() with a decision model, keeping the same 1 to 5 urgency output and the existing rule that free-plan tickets never rate 5.
implement.input_shape: the InboundTicket object passed to rateUrgency()

samples.subject: Production API returning 500 for all requests
samples.body: Since 09:10 UTC every call to /v1/orders returns 500. Our checkout is down and we are losing sales. Enterprise account.

samples.subject: Dark mode?
samples.body: Any plans for a dark mode in the dashboard? Not urgent, just curious.

rubric.text: Uses a score (or a choice over the five levels) whose criteria describe each urgency level as a concrete situation, rather than a noul or a free number.
The rule that free-plan tickets cap at 4 is applied in code after the answer, not by telling the model about the plan or asking it to apply the cap.
The typed answer is read directly (score, probabilities, or choice) with no text parsing.

sites.why: Token-overlap similarity with a tuned threshold standing in for the judgment of whether a new ticket reports the same issue as an open one.

implement.brief: Replace the Jaccard similarity in findDuplicate() with a decision model that picks which open ticket, if any, the new ticket duplicates.
implement.input_shape: an object { ticket: InboundTicket, open: OpenTicket[] } with the same fields as the function parameters

rubric.text: The open tickets are placed in state keyed by ticket id (or otherwise named so each option can be referred to directly), not as an array the model must index into.
A none / no duplicate option exists (as a choice option or as a separate presence noul) so the model is not forced to pick a candidate.
Filtering to status === open and limiting the candidate count stays in code.
When there are no open candidates the code returns none without calling the model.

sites.why: Word lists and regexes standing in for independent semantic labels (profanity, promotional, harassment) that can co-occur.

implement.brief: Replace the word lists and promo regexes in moderate() with a decision model, keeping the same flags and publish decision.
implement.input_shape: the ProductReview object passed to moderate()

samples.title: Broke after a week
samples.body: The strap snapped after seven days. Support was slow to respond. Would not buy again.

samples.title: Great but cheaper elsewhere
samples.body: Love it. If you want 20% off go to my page and message me for the code.

rubric.text: Profanity, promotional, and harassment are separate noul questions (labels can co-occur), not a single choice.
The too_short check on body length stays in code and is not asked of the model.
Questions ask whether the review is promotional or harassing, not whether it contains a URL, a discount code, or particular words.

sites.why: Manual review queue where the hard policy rules are already in code and the only remaining work is a semantic read of the reason text against covered reasons.

implement.brief: Change decideRefund() so requests under the auto-approve cap are approved or denied from the reason text against the policy (damaged, defective, wrong item, or undelivered qualify, change of mind does not), and only unclear cases go to manual_review.
implement.input_shape: the RefundRequest object passed to decideRefund()

samples.reason: The mug arrived with a crack down one side and leaks.
Decided I do not need it after all.
Screen has dead pixels out of the box.

rubric.text: The 30 day window, undelivered auto-approve, previous refund count, and amount cap remain code checks that run before the model.
When a hard rule already settles the outcome (outside window, undelivered, over cap, too many refunds) the code returns without calling the model.
State sent to the model is the reason text (plus at most what a question needs), not the amounts, dates, or counts code already used.

There is an explicit path to manual_review for reasons the model finds unclear (via a no-match / unclear option or a confidence or probability gate in code), rather than every case being forced to approve or deny.

sites.why: Keyword if-chain over free text standing in for a routing judgment, with deterministic rules (source, employee count) mixed in.

implement.brief: Replace the keyword if-chain in routeLead() with a decision model, keeping the same team outputs and the existing source and employee-count rules.
implement.input_shape: the Lead object passed to routeLead()

samples.message: We want to embed your reporting in our own product and resell it to our customers under our brand.
Hi, how do I authenticate against the REST endpoints from a Node service? Docs are unclear.
Introduced by your partner team at the summit. Interested in a joint go to market.

rubric.text: The partner source and employee-count rules run in code before the model and return without calling it.
Uses one choice over the teams including general_inbox (or an equivalent none option).
The model is not asked to judge company size from the employee count that code already compared.

sites.why: Embedding similarity threshold standing in for the judgment of whether the top retrieved article actually answers the ticket.

implement.brief: Keep the embedding retrieval in suggestArticle() but replace the similarity threshold with a decision model that picks which of the retrieved articles, if any, answers the ticket.
implement.input_shape: an object { ticket: InboundTicket, candidates: Array<{ slug, title, summary }> } holding the top retrieved articles

rubric.text: Embedding, cosine ranking, and the top-k cut stay in code. The model only judges the retrieved candidates.
Candidates are in state keyed by slug (or otherwise named per option) with title and summary, and each option in the question names its article.
A none option (or separate does-any-article-answer noul) exists so an unrelated set of articles yields no suggestion.
The cosine similarity numbers are not sent to the model for it to weigh.

sites.why: Business-hours arithmetic and date comparison. Fully deterministic.
Exact pattern validation and map lookup. Nothing semantic to judge.
Role and MFA rules already expressed as data. A model must never decide authorization.
Template interpolation. Producing text is generation, not a decision.
HMAC signature and timestamp checks. Exact matching with security consequences.
